Starting temperature (Kelvin) in FCP dynamics runs
target temperature for most thermostats.

FCP.name: fcp_tolp
FCP.label: Tolerance for FCP velocity rescaling
FCP.description:
Tolerance for velocity rescaling. Velocities are rescaled if
the run-averaged and target temperature differ more than tolp.

FCP.name: fcp_delta_t
FCP.label: FCP temperature rescaling
FCP.description:
if "fcp_temperature" == 'rescale-T' :
at each step the instantaneous temperature is multiplied
by fcp_delta_t; this is done rescaling all the velocities.

if "fcp_temperature" == 'reduce-T' :
every "fcp_nraise" steps the instantaneous temperature is
reduced by -"fcp_delta_t" (i.e. "fcp_delta_t" < 0 is added to T)

The instantaneous temperature is calculated at the end of
FCP's move and BEFORE rescaling. This is the temperature
reported in the main output.

For "fcp_delta_t" < 0, the actual average rate of heating or cooling
should be roughly C*fcp_delta_t/(fcp_nraise*dt) (C=1 for an
ideal gas, C=0.5 for a harmonic solid, theorem of energy
equipartition between all quadratic degrees of freedom).

FCP.name: fcp_nraise
FCP.label: FCP rescaling interval

FCP.name: freeze_all_atoms
FCP.label: Freeze all atoms in FCP dynamics
FCP.description:
If .TRUE., freeze all atoms
to perform relaxation or dynamics only with FCP.

RISM.name: nsolv
RISM.label: Number of solvents
RISM.description: The number of solvents (i.e. molecular species) in the unit cell

RISM.name: closure
RISM.label: Type of closure equation
RISM.description:
Specify the type of closure equation:

'kh' :

The Kovalenko and Hirata's model.
[A.Kovalenko, F.Hirata, JCP 110, 10095 (1999), "doi:10.1063/1.478883"]

'hnc' :

The HyperNetted-Chain model, which is
suitable only for solvents without charge.
[J.P.Hansen et al., Theory of simple liquids. Academic Press, London, 1990]

RISM.name: tempv
RISM.label: Solvent temperature in Kelvin
RISM.description: Temperature (Kelvin) of solvents.

RISM.name: ecutsolv
RISM.label: Energy cutoff for 3D-RISM in Rydberg
RISM.description:
Kinetic energy cutoff (Ry) for solvent's correlation functions.
If a solute is an isolated system or slab, you may allowed to
use default value. For a frameworked or porous solute (e.g. Zeolite, MOF),
it is desirable to apply a larger value. Solvents confined in a framework
often have a high frequency.

RISM.name: solute_lj
RISM.label: Type of Lennard-Jones force fields for solutes
RISM.description:
Specify the Lennard-Jones potential of solute on atomic type 'i':

'none' :

The Lennard-Jones potential is not specified here.
you must set "solute_epsilon" and "solute_sigma".

'uff' :

Universal Force Field.
[A.K.Rappe et al., JACS 144, 10024 (1992), "doi:10.1021/ja00051a040"]

'clayff' :

Clay's Force Field
[R.T.Cygan et al., JPC B 108, 1255 (2004), "doi:10.1021/jp0363287"]

'opls-aa' :

OPLS-AA (generic parameters for QM/MM)

RISM.name: solute_epsilon
RISM.label: Lennard-Jones `epsilon' parameters for solutes [in kcal/mol]
RISM.description:
The Lennard-Jones potential of solute on atomic type 'i'.
Here, you can set the parameter 'epsilon' (kcal/mol).

RISM.name: solute_sigma
RISM.label: Lennard-Jones `sigma' parameters for solutes [in Angstroms]
RISM.description:
The Lennard-Jones potential of solute on atomic type 'i'.
Here, you can set the parameter 'sigma' (Angstrom).

RISM.name: starting1d
RISM.label: How to initialize the 1D-RISM's correlation function
RISM.description:
'zero' :

Starting correlation functions of 1D-RISM from zero.
( default for scf, *relax, *md )

'file' :

Start from existing "1d-rism_csvv_r.xml" file in the
directory specified by variables "prefix" and "outdir".

'fix' :

Read from existing "1d-rism_csvv_r.xml" file in the
directory specified by variables "prefix" and "outdir",
and never calculate 1D-RISM.
For nscf and bands calculation this is the default.

RISM.name: smear1d
RISM.label: Smearing radius for 1D-RISM [in Bohr]
RISM.description: Coulomb smearing radius (a.u.) for 1D-RISM.

RISM.name: rism1d_maxstep
RISM.label: Maximum number of steps for 1D-RISM
RISM.description: Maximum number of iterations in a 1D-RISM step.

RISM.name: rism1d_conv_thr
RISM.label: Convergence threshold for 1D-RISM
RISM.description: Convergence threshold for 1D-RISM.

RISM.name: mdiis1d_size
RISM.label: Size of MDIIS for 1D-RISM
RISM.description: Size of Modified DIIS (MDIIS) for 1D-RISM.

RISM.name: mdiis1d_step
RISM.label: Step of MDIIS for 1D-RISM
RISM.description: Step of Modified DIIS (MDIIS) for 1D-RISM.

RISM.name: rism1d_bond_width
RISM.label: Gaussian width of bonds for 1D-RISM
RISM.description:
Gaussian width of bonds to smear intra-molecular correlation for 1D-RISM.
If 3D-RISM calculation, default is 0.
If Laue-RISM calculation, default is 2 / SQRT("ecutwfc").

RISM.name: rism1d_dielectric
RISM.label: Dielectric constant for 1D-RISM
RISM.description:
Dielectric constant for 1D-RISM.
If "rism1d_dielectric" > 0, dielectrically consistent RISM (DRISM) is performed.

For details of DRISM, see:
J.S.Perkyns and B.M.Pettitt, CPL 1992, 190, 626, "doi:10.1016/0009-2614(92)85201-K"

RISM.name: rism1d_molesize
RISM.label:
Size of solvent molecule for 1D-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
Size of solvent molecules (a.u.) for 1D-RISM.
This is used only if "rism1d_dielectric" > 0.
If you have large molecules, you have to set ~ 20 a.u. .

RISM.name: rism1d_nproc
RISM.label: Number of processes to calculate for 1D-RISM
RISM.description: Number of processes to calculate 1D-RISM.

RISM.name: starting3d
RISM.label: How to initialize the 3D-RISM's correlation function
RISM.description:
'zero' :

Starting correlation functions of 3D-RISM from zero.
( default for scf, *relax, *md )

'file' :

Start from existing "3d-rism_csuv_r.dat" file in the
directory specified by variables "prefix" and "outdir".
For nscf and bands calculation this is the default.

RISM.name: smear3d
RISM.label: Smearing radius for 3D-RISM [in Bohr]
RISM.description: Coulomb smearing radius (a.u.) for 3D-RISM.

RISM.name: rism3d_maxstep
RISM.label: Maximum number of steps for 3D-RISM
RISM.description: Maximum number of iterations in a 3D-RISM step.

RISM.name: rism3d_conv_thr
RISM.label: Convergence threshold for 3D-RISM
RISM.description: Convergence threshold for 3D-RISM.

RISM.name: mdiis3d_size
RISM.label: Size of MDIIS for 3D-RISM
RISM.description: Size of Modified DIIS (MDIIS) for 3D-RISM.

RISM.name: mdiis3d_step
RISM.label: Step of MDIIS for 3D-RISM
RISM.description: Step of Modified DIIS (MDIIS) for 3D-RISM.

RISM.name: rism3d_conv_level
RISM.label: Convergence level for 3D-RISM
RISM.description:
Convergence level of 3D-RISM.

0.0 :

Convergence level is 'low'.
Convergence threshold of 3D-RISM is greater than
"rism3d_conv_thr", when estimated energy error >> "conv_thr" .
The threshold becomes "rism3d_conv_thr", when
estimated energy error is enough small.

0.0<x<1.0 :

Convergence level is 'medium'.
Convergence threshold of 3D-RISM is intermediate value
between 'low' and 'high', where "rism3d_conv_level" is mixing rate.

1.0 :

Convergence level is 'high'.
Convergence threshold of 3D-RISM is always "rism3d_conv_thr" .

RISM.name: rism3d_planar_average
RISM.label:
Calculate planar average of solvents after 3D-RISM 
calculation
RISM.description:
If .TRUE., planar averages of solvent densities and potentials
are calculated and written to 'prefix.rism1'.
For 3D-RISM, default is .FALSE.
For Laue-RISM, default is .TRUE.

RISM.name: laue_both_hands
RISM.label: Use both-hands method in Laue-RISM
RISM.description:
If .TRUE., you can set different densities
to the solvent regions of right-hand side and left-hand side.
See "SOLVENTS" card.

RISM.name: laue_nfit
RISM.label: Number of fitting points in Laue-RISM
RISM.description:
The number of z-grid points for the polynomial fit along the cell edge.
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_expand_right
RISM.label:
Expanding length on right-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
If positive value, set the ending position offset [in a.u.]
of the solvent region on right-hand side of the unit cell,
measured relative to the unit cell edge.
(the solvent region ends at z = + [L_z/2 + "laue_expand_right"].)
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_expand_left
RISM.label:
Expanding length on left-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
If positive value, set the ending position offset [in a.u.]
of the solvent region on left-hand side of the unit cell,
measured relative to the unit cell edge.
(the solvent region ends at z = - [L_z/2 + "laue_expand_left"].)
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_starting_right
RISM.label:
Starting position on right-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
Set the starting position [in a.u.] of the solvent region
on right-hand side of the unit cell. Then the solvent region is
defined as [ "laue_starting_right" , L_z/2 + "laue_expand_right" ],
where distribution functions are finite.
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_starting_left
RISM.label:
Starting position on left-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
Set the starting position [in a.u.] of the solvent region
on left-hand side of the unit cell. Then the solvent region is
defined as [ -L_z/2 - "laue_expand_left" , "laue_starting_left" ],
where distribution functions are finite.
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_buffer_right
RISM.label:
Buffering length on right-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
If positive value, set the buffering length [in a.u.]
of the solvent region on right-hand side of the unit cell.
Then correlation functions are defined inside of
[ "laue_starting_right" - "laue_buffer_right" , L_z/2 + "laue_expand_right" ].
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_buffer_left
RISM.label:
Buffering length on left-hand side in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
If positive value, set the buffering length [in a.u.]
of the solvent region on left-hand side of the unit cell.
Then correlation functions are defined inside of
[ -L_z/2 - "laue_expand_left" , "laue_starting_left" + "laue_buffer_left" ].
This is only for Laue-RISM.

RISM.name: laue_wall
RISM.label:
Repulsive wall with (1/r)^12 term of Lennard-Jones 
potential
RISM.description:
Set the repulsive wall with (1/r)^12 term of Lennard-Jones potential.
This is only for Laue-RISM.

'none' :

The repulsive wall is not defined.

'auto' :

The repulsive wall is defined, whose edge position is set automatically.
One does not have to set "laue_wall_z" (the edge position).

'manual' :

The repulsive wall is defined, whose edge position is set manually.
One have to set "laue_wall_z" (the edge position).

RISM.name: laue_wall_z
RISM.label:
Edge position of repulsive wall in Laue-RISM 
[in Bohr]
RISM.description:
Set the edge position [in a.u.] of the repulsive wall.
If "laue_expand_right" > 0.0, the repulsive wall is defined on [ -inf , "laue_wall_z" ].
If "laue_expand_left" > 0.0, the repulsive wall is defined on [ "laue_wall_z" , inf ].
This is only for Laue-RISM and "laue_wall" == 'manual' .

RISM.name: laue_wall_rho
RISM.label:
Density of repulsive wall in Laue-RISM 
[in 1/Bohr^3]
RISM.description:
The density (1/bohr^3) of the repulsive wall.
This is only for Laue-RISM and "laue_wall" /= 'none' .

RISM.name: laue_wall_epsilon
RISM.label:
Lennard-Jones parameter `epsilon' for repulsive wall 
in Laue-RISM [in kcal/mol]
RISM.description:
The Lennard-Jones potential of the repulsive wall.
Here, you can set the parameter 'epsilon' (kcal/mol).
This is only for Laue-RISM and "laue_wall" /= 'none' .

RISM.name: laue_wall_sigma
RISM.label:
Lennard-Jones parameters `sigma' for repulsive wall 
in Laue-RISM [in Angstrom]
RISM.description:
The Lennard-Jones potential of the repulsive wall.
Here, you can set the parameter 'sigma' (Angstrom).
This is only for Laue-RISM and "laue_wall" /= 'none' .

RISM.name: laue_wall_lj6
RISM.label: Use attractive term of Lennard-Jones
RISM.description:
If .TRUE., the attractive term -(1/r)^6 of Lennard-Jones potential is added.
This is only for Laue-RISM and "laue_wall" /= 'none' .

INPUTPH.name: outdir
INPUTPH.label: Temporary directory where punch file resides
INPUTPH.default:
value of the ESPRESSO_TMPDIR environment variable if set;

current directory ('./') otherwise

INPUTPH.name: prefix
INPUTPH.label: Prefix of data file saved by PW.X
INPUTPH.description:
Prepended to input/output filenames; must be the same
used in the calculation of unperturbed system.

INPUTPH.name: dftd3_hess
INPUTPH.label: File containing D3 dispersion Hessian matrix
INPUTPH.description:
File where the D3 dispersion hessian matrix is read. Set to
'automatic.hess' to enable automatic mode (experimental). In
this mode, D3 Hessian is computed if 'automatic.hess' file is
missing.

INPUTPH.name: fildyn
INPUTPH.label: File containing the dynamical matrix
INPUTPH.description: File where the dynamical matrix is written.

INPUTPH.name: fildrho
INPUTPH.label: File containing the charge density variations
INPUTPH.description:
File where the charge density responses are written. Note that the file
will actually be saved as ${outdir}/_ph0/${prefix}.${fildrho}1
where  ${outdir}, ${prefix} and ${fildrho} are the values of the
corresponding input variables

INPUTPH.name: fildvscf
INPUTPH.label: File containing the potential variation
INPUTPH.description:
File where the the potential variation is written
(for later use in electron-phonon calculation, see also fildrho).

INPUTPH.name: ldisp
INPUTPH.label: Compute phonon dispersions
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. the run calculates phonons for a grid of
q-points specified by "nq1", "nq2", "nq3" - for direct
calculation of the entire phonon dispersion.

INPUTPH.name: nogg
INPUTPH.label: Disable gamma_gamma tricks
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. disable the "gamma_gamma" trick used to speed
up calculations at q=0 (phonon wavevector) if the sum over
the Brillouin Zone includes k=0 only. The gamma_gamma
trick exploits symmetry and acoustic sum rule to reduce
the number of linear response calculations to the strict
minimum, as it is done in code phcg.x.

INPUTPH.name: asr
INPUTPH.label: Apply acoustic sum rule for "gamma_gamma"
INPUTPH.description:
Apply Acoustic Sum Rule to dynamical matrix, effective charges
Works only in conjunction with "gamma_gamma" tricks (see above)

INPUTPH.name: ldiag
INPUTPH.label: Force diagonalization of the incomplete dynamical matrix
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. forces the diagonalization of the dynamical
matrix also when only a part of the dynamical matrix
has been calculated. It is used together with "start_irr"
and "last_irr". If all modes corresponding to a
given irreducible representation have been calculated,
the phonon frequencies of that representation are
correct. The others are zero or wrong. Use with care.

INPUTPH.name: trans
INPUTPH.label: Compute phonons for a single q vector
INPUTPH.description:
If .false. the phonons are not computed.
If "trans" .and. "epsil" are both .true.,
the effective charges are calculated.
If "ldisp" is .true., "trans"=.false. is overridden
(except for the case of electron-phonon calculations)

INPUTPH.name: epsil
INPUTPH.label: Compute the macroscopic dielectric constant for q=0
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. in a q=0 calculation for a non metal the
macroscopic dielectric constant of the system is
computed. Do not set "epsil" to .true. if you have a
metallic system or q/=0: the code will complain and stop.

Note: the input value of "epsil" will be ignored if "ldisp"=.true.
(the code will automatically set "epsil" to .false. for metals,
to .true. for insulators: see routine PHonon/PH/prepare_q.f90).

INPUTPH.name: electron_phonon
INPUTPH.label: Compute electron-phonon
INPUTPH.description:
Options are:

'simple' :

Electron-phonon lambda coefficients are computed
for a given q and a grid of k-points specified by
the variables "nk1", "nk2", "nk3", "k1", "k2", "k3".

'interpolated' :

Electron-phonon is calculated by interpolation
over the Brillouin Zone as in M. Wierzbowska, et
al. "arXiv:cond-mat/0504077"

'lambda_tetra' :

The electron-phonon coefficient \lambda_{q \nu}
is calculated with the optimized tetrahedron method.

'gamma_tetra' :

The phonon linewidth \gamma_{q \nu} is calculated
from the electron-phonon interactions
using the optimized tetrahedron method.

'epa' :

Electron-phonon coupling matrix elements are written
to file prefix.epa.k for further processing by program
epa.x which implements electron-phonon averaged (EPA)
approximation as described in G. Samsonidze & B. Kozinsky,
Adv. Energy Mater. 2018, 1800246 "doi:10.1002/aenm.201800246"
"arXiv:1511.08115"

'ahc' :

Quantities required for the calculation of phonon-induced
electron self-energy are computed and written to the directory
"ahc_dir". The output files can be read by postahc.x for
the calculation of electron self-energy.
Available for both metals and insulators.
"trans"=.false. is required.

For metals only, requires gaussian smearing (except for 'ahc').

If "trans"=.true., the lambdas are calculated in the same
run, using the same k-point grid for phonons and lambdas.
If "trans"=.false., the lambdas are calculated using
previously saved DeltaVscf in "fildvscf", previously saved
dynamical matrix, and the present punch file. This allows
the use of a different (larger) k-point grid.

INPUTPH.name: el_ph_nsigma
INPUTPH.label: The number of double-delta smearing values
INPUTPH.description:
The number of double-delta smearing values used in an
electron-phonon coupling calculation.

INPUTPH.name: el_ph_sigma
INPUTPH.label: The spacing between double-delta smearing values
INPUTPH.description:
The spacing between double-delta smearing values used in
an electron-phonon coupling calculation.

INPUTPH.name: ahc_dir
INPUTPH.label: Directory for the output ahc files
INPUTPH.description: Directory where the output binary files are written.

INPUTPH.name: ahc_nbnd
INPUTPH.label: Number of bands for the electron self-energy
INPUTPH.description: Number of bands for which the electron self-energy is to be computed.

INPUTPH.name: ahc_nbndskip
INPUTPH.label: Number of bands to exclude from self-energy
INPUTPH.description:
Number of bands to exclude when computing the self-energy. Self-energy
is computed for bands with indices from "ahc_nbndskip"+1 to
"ahc_nbndskip"+"ahc_nbnd". "ahc_nbndskip"+"ahc_nbnd" cannot
exceed nbnd of the preceding SCF or NSCF calculation.

INPUTPH.name: skip_upperfan
INPUTPH.label: Skip calculation of the upper Fan self-energy
INPUTPH.description:
If .true., skip calculation of the upper Fan self-energy, which
involves solving the Sternheimer equation.

INPUTPH.name: lrpa
INPUTPH.label: Compute dielectric constant with RPA and dV_xc=0
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. the dielectric constant is calculated at the
RPA level with DV_xc=0.

INPUTPH.name: lnoloc
INPUTPH.label: Compute dielectric constant with dV_H=0 and  dV_xc=0
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. the dielectric constant is calculated without
local fields, i.e. by setting DV_H=0 and DV_xc=0.

INPUTPH.name: fpol
INPUTPH.label: Compute dynamic polarizabilities
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. calculate dynamic polarizabilities
Requires "epsil"=.true. ( experimental stage:
see example09 for calculation of methane ).

INPUTPH.name: lshift_q
INPUTPH.label: Use a wave-vector half-step grid displaced
INPUTPH.description:
Use a wave-vector grid displaced by half a grid step
in each direction - meaningful only when ldisp is .true.
When this option is set, the q2r.x code cannot be used.

INPUTPH.name: zeu
INPUTPH.label: Compute effective charges from the dielectric responses
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. in a q=0 calculation for a non metal the
effective charges are computed from the dielectric
response. This is the default algorithm. If "epsil"=.true.
and "zeu"=.false. only the dielectric tensor is calculated.

INPUTPH.name: zue
INPUTPH.label: Compute effective charges from the phonon density responses
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. in a q=0 calculation for a non metal the
effective charges are computed from the phonon
density responses. This is an alternative algorithm,
different from the default one (if "trans" .and. "epsil" )
The results should be the same within numerical noise.

INPUTPH.name: elop
INPUTPH.label: Compute electro-optic coefficients
INPUTPH.description: If .true. calculate electro-optic tensor.

INPUTPH.name: lraman
INPUTPH.label: Compute Raman coefficients

INPUTPH.name: search_sym
INPUTPH.label: Perform mode symmetry analysis
INPUTPH.description:
Set it to .false. if you want to disable the mode
symmetry analysis.

INPUTPH.name: eth_rps
INPUTPH.label: Threshold for calculation of x|Psi>
INPUTPH.description: Threshold for calculation of  Pc R |psi>.

INPUTPH.name: eth_ns
INPUTPH.label: Threshold for non-scf wavefunction calculation
INPUTPH.description: Threshold for non-scf wavefunction calculation.

INPUTPH.name: dek
INPUTPH.label: Delta k used for wavefunction derivation wtr k (dek)
INPUTPH.description: Delta_xk used for wavefunction derivation wrt k.

INPUTPH.name: dvscf_star
INPUTPH.label: dvscf_star

INPUTPH.name: dvscf_star_open
INPUTPH.label: Compute potential variations at all q-points in the star

INPUTPH.description:
If .true. three q points and relative weights are
read from input. The three q points define the rectangle
q(:,1) + l (q(:,2)-q(:,1)) + m (q(:,3)-q(:,1)) where
0< l,m < 1. The weights are integer and those of points two
and three are the number of points in the two directions.

q(:,i) define the line from q(:,i) to q(:,i+1) and nq
points are generated along that line. nq is the weigth of
q(:,i). When .false. only the list of q points given as
input is calculated. The weights are not used.

INPUTPH.name: lqdir
INPUTPH.label: Creates inside outdir a separate subdirectory for each q vector
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. ph.x creates inside outdir a separate subdirectory
for each q vector. The flag is set to .true. when "ldisp"=.true.
and "fildvscf" /= ' ' or when an electron-phonon
calculation is performed. The induced potential is saved
separately for each q inside the subdirectories.

INPUTPH.description:
Perform calculations only from "start_irr" to "last_irr"
irreducible representations.

* do not specify "nat_todo" together with
"start_irr", "last_irr"

INPUTPH.name: last_irr
INPUTPH.label: Last irreducible representations in range
INPUTPH.description:
Perform calculations only from "start_irr" to "last_irr"
irreducible representations.

IMPORTANT:
* "start_irr" must be <= 3*nat
* do not specify "nat_todo" together with
"start_irr", "last_irr"

INPUTPH.name: nat_todo
INPUTPH.label: Number of atom to be displaced
INPUTPH.description:
Choose the subset of atoms to be used in the linear response
calculation: "nat_todo" atoms, specified in input (see below)
are displaced. Can be used to estimate modes for a molecule
adsorbed over a surface without performing a full fledged
calculation. Use with care, at your own risk, and be aware
that this is an approximation and may not work.
IMPORTANT:
* "nat_todo" <= nat
* if linear-response is calculated for a given atom, it
should also be done for all symmetry-equivalent atoms,
or else you will get incorrect results

INPUTPH.name: modenum
INPUTPH.label: Index of the irreducible representation for single-mode calculation
INPUTPH.description:
For single-mode phonon calculation : modenum is the index of the
irreducible representation (irrep) into which the reducible
representation formed by the 3*nat atomic displacements are
decomposed in order to perform the phonon calculation.
Note that a single-mode calculation will not give you the
frequency of a single phonon mode: in general, the selected
"modenum" is not an eigenvector. What you get on output is
a column of the dynamical matrix.

INPUTPH.name: start_q

INPUTPH.description:

Computes only the q points from "start_q" to "last_q".

IMPORTANT:

* do not specify "nat_todo" together with

INPUTPH.name: last_q
INPUTPH.label: Last q-point in range
INPUTPH.description:
Used only when "ldisp"=.true..
Computes only the q points from "start_q" to "last_q".

IMPORTANT

* do not specify "nat_todo" together with
"start_q", "last_q"

INPUTPH.name: diagonalization
INPUTPH.label: Diagonalization method for the non-SCF
INPUTPH.description:
Diagonalization method for the non-SCF calculations.

'david' :

Davidson iterative diagonalization with overlap matrix
(default). Fast, may in some rare cases fail.

'cg' :

Conjugate-gradient-like band-by-band diagonalization.
Slower than 'david' but uses less memory and is
(a little bit) more robust.

INPUTPH.name: read_dns_bare
INPUTPH.label: For DFPT+U: read the dns_* files
INPUTPH.description:
If .true. the PH code tries to read three files in the DFPT+U
calculation: dns_orth, dns_bare, d2ns_bare.
dns_orth and dns_bare are the first-order variations of
the occupation matrix, while d2ns_bare is the second-order
variation of the occupation matrix. These matrices are
computed only once during the DFPT+U calculation. However,
their calculation (especially of d2ns_bare) is computationally
expensive, this is why they are written to file and then can be
read (e.g. for restart) in order to save time.

INPUTPH.name: ldvscf_interpolate
INPUTPH.label: Use Fourier interpolation of phonon potential
INPUTPH.description:
If .true., use Fourier interpolation of phonon potential
to compute the induced part of phonon potential at each
q point. Results of a dvscf_q2r.x run is needed.
Requires "trans" = .false..

INPUTPH.name: wpot_dir
INPUTPH.label: Directory for the w_pot binary files
INPUTPH.description:
Directory where the w_pot binary files are written.
Must be the same with "wpot_dir" used in dvscf_q2r.x.
The real space potential files are stored in "wpot_dir"
with names ${prefix}.wpot.irc${irc}//"1".

INPUTPH.name: do_long_range
INPUTPH.label: Add the long-range part of the potential
INPUTPH.description:
If .true., add the long-range part of the potential
to the Fourier interpolated potential as in:
S. Ponce et al, J. Chem. Phys. 143, 102813 (2015).
Reads dielectric matrix and Born effective charges from
the ${wpot_dir}/tensors.dat file, written in dvscf_q2r.x.
Currently, only the dipole (Frohlich) part is implemented.
The quadrupole part is not implemented.

INPUTPH.name: do_charge_neutral
INPUTPH.label: Impose charge neutrality on the Born effective charges
INPUTPH.description:
If .true., impose charge neutrality on the Born effective
charges. Used only if "do_long_range" = .true..

INPUTPP.name: plot_num
INPUTPP.label: What to calculate
INPUTPP.description:
Selects what to save in filplot:

0  = electron (pseudo-)charge density

1  = total potential V_bare + V_H + V_xc

2  = local ionic potential V_bare

3  = local density of states at specific energy or grid of energies
(number of states per volume, in bohr^3, per energy unit, in Ry)

4  = local density of electronic entropy

5  = STM images
Tersoff and Hamann, "PRB 31, 805 (1985)"

6  = spin polarization (rho(up)-rho(down))

7  = contribution of selected wavefunction(s) to the
(pseudo-)charge density. For norm-conserving PPs,
|psi|^2 (psi=selected wavefunction). Noncollinear case:
contribution of the given state to the charge or
to the magnetization along the direction indicated
by spin_component (0 = charge, 1 = x, 2 = y, 3 = z )

8  = electron localization function (ELF)

9  = charge density minus superposition of atomic densities

10 = integrated local density of states (ILDOS)
from "emin" to "emax" (emin, emax in eV)
if "emax" is not specified, "emax"=E_fermi

11 = the V_bare + V_H potential

12 = the sawtooth electric field potential (if present)

13 = the noncollinear magnetization.

17 = all-electron valence charge density
can be performed for PAW calculations only
requires a very dense real-space grid!

18 = The exchange and correlation magnetic field in the noncollinear case

19 = Reduced density gradient
( J. Chem. Theory Comput. 7, 625 (2011), "doi:10.1021/ct100641a" )
Set the isosurface between 0.3 and 0.6 to plot the
non-covalent interactions (see also plot_num = 20)

20 = Product of the electron density (charge) and the second
eigenvalue of the electron-density Hessian matrix;
used to colorize the RDG plot (plot_num = 19)

21 = all-electron charge density (valence+core).
For PAW calculations only; requires a very dense real-space grid.

22 = kinetic energy density (for meta-GGA and XDM only)

123 = DORI: density overlap regions indicator
("doi: 10.1021/ct500490b") Implemented by D. Yang & Q.Liu

is written, for usage by "plotband.x"

BANDS.name: no_overlap
BANDS.label: Don't change the order of eigenvalues in output file
BANDS.description:
If .false., and if "lsym" is .false., writes the eigenvalues
in the order that maximises overlap with the neighbor k-points

BANDS.name: plot_2d
BANDS.label: Print the eigenvalues in 2D gnuplot's format
BANDS.description:
If .true. writes the eigenvalues in the output file
in a 2D format readable by gnuplot. Band ordering is not
changed. Each band is written in a different file called
filband.# with the format:

xk, yk, energy
xk, yk, energy
..  ..  ..

energies are written in eV and xk in units 2\pi/a.

INPUTHP.name: prefix
INPUTHP.label: Prefix of outdir files saved by program PW.X
INPUTHP.description:
Prepended to input/output filenames; must be the same
used in the calculation of unperturbed system.

INPUTHP.name: outdir
INPUTHP.label: Outdir directory where PW.X files resides
INPUTHP.default:
value of the ESPRESSO_TMPDIR environment variable if set;

current directory ('./') otherwise

INPUTHP.name: iverbosity
INPUTHP.label: Verbosity
INPUTHP.description:
= 1 : minimal output
= 2 : as above + symmetry matrices, final response
matrices chi0 and chi1 and their inverse matrices,
full U matrix
= 3 : as above + various detailed info about the NSCF
calculation at k and k+q
= 4 : as above + response occupation matrices at every
iteration and for every q point in the star

INPUTHP.name: max_seconds
INPUTHP.label: Maximum CPU time [in seconds]
INPUTHP.description: Maximum allowed run time before the job stops smoothly.

INPUTHP.name: nq1
INPUTHP.label: nq1

INPUTHP.name: nq2
INPUTHP.label: nq2

INPUTHP.name: nq3
INPUTHP.label: nq3

INPUTHP.name: skip_equivalence_q
INPUTHP.label: Skip the equivalence analysis of q points
INPUTHP.description:
If .true. then the HP code will skip the equivalence
analysis of q points, and thus the full grid of q points
will be used. Otherwise the symmetry is used to determine
equivalent q points (star of q), and then perform
calculations only for inequivalent q points.

INPUTHP.name: start_q
INPUTHP.label: First q-point
INPUTHP.description:
Computes only the q points from "start_q" to "last_q".

IMPORTANT: "start_q" must be smaller or equal to
the total number of q points found.

INPUTHP.name: last_q
INPUTHP.label: Last q-point
INPUTHP.description:
Computes only the q points from "start_q" to "last_q".

IMPORTANT: "last_q" must be smaller or equal to
the total number of q points found.

INPUTHP.name: sum_pertq
INPUTHP.label: Collect pieces of the response occupation matrices
INPUTHP.description:
If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect
pieces of the response occupation matrices for all
q points. This variable should be used only when
"start_q", "last_q" and "perturb_only_atom" are used.

INPUTHP.name: determine_num_pert_only
INPUTHP.label: Only determine the number of perturbations
INPUTHP.description:
If .true. determines the number of perturbations
(i.e. which atoms will be perturbed) and exits smoothly
without performing any calculation. For DFT+U+V, it also
determines the indices of inter-site couples.

INPUTHP.name: determine_q_mesh_only
INPUTHP.label: Only determine the number of q points
INPUTHP.description:
If .true. determines the number of q points
for a given perturbed atom and exits smoothly.
This keyword can be used only if perturb_only_atom
is set to .true.

INPUTHP.name: find_atpert
INPUTHP.label: Method for searching which atoms must be perturbed
INPUTHP.description:
Method for searching of atoms which must be perturbed.
1 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms there are
by analyzing unperturbed occupations.
2 = Find how many Hubbard atoms to perturb based on
how many different Hubbard atomic types there are.
Warning: atoms which have the same type but which
are inequivalent by symmetry or which have different
occupations will not be distinguished in this case
(use option 1 or 3 instead).
3 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms
there are using symmetry. Atoms which have the
same type but are not equivalent by symmetry will
be distinguished in this case.
4 = Perturb all Hubbard atoms (the most expensive option)

INPUTHP.name: docc_thr
INPUTHP.label: Threshold for a comparison of unperturbed occupations
INPUTHP.description:
Threshold for a comparison of unperturbed occupations
which is needed for the selection of atoms which must
be perturbed. Can be used only when "find_atpert" = 1.

INPUTHP.name: skip_type
INPUTHP.label: Skip i-th atom-type in linear-response calculation
INPUTHP.description:
"skip_type"(i), where i runs over types of atoms.
If "skip_type"(i)=.true. then no linear-response
calculation will be performed for the i-th atomic type:
in this case "equiv_type"(i) must be specified, otherwise
the HP code will stop. This option is useful if the
system has atoms of the same type but opposite spin
pollarizations (anti-ferromagnetic case).
This keyword cannot be used when "find_atpert" = 1.

INPUTHP.name: equiv_type
INPUTHP.label: Make atom-type i equivalent to atom-type j
INPUTHP.description:
"equiv_type"(i), where i runs over types of atoms.
"equiv_type"(i)=j, will make type i equivalent to type j
(useful when nspin=2). Such a merging of types is done
only at the post-processing stage.
This keyword cannot be used when "find_atpert" = 1.

INPUTHP.name: perturb_only_atom
INPUTHP.label: Perturb only i-th atom types
INPUTHP.description:
If "perturb_only_atom"(i)=.true. then only the i-th
atom will be perturbed and considered in the run.
This variable is useful when one wants to split
the whole calculation on parts.

Note: this variable has a higher priority than "skip_type".

INPUTHP.name: compute_hp
INPUTHP.label: Collect pieces of the chi0 and chi matrices
INPUTHP.description:
If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect
pieces of the chi0 and chi matrices (which must have
been produced in previous runs) and then compute
Hubbard parameters. The HP code will look for files
tmp_dir/HP/prefix.chi.i.dat. Note that all files
prefix.chi.i.dat (where i runs over all perturbed
atoms) must be placed in one folder tmp_dir/HP/.
"compute_hp"=.true. must be used only when the
calculation was parallelized over perturbations.

INPUTHP.name: conv_thr_chi
INPUTHP.label: Convergence threshold for the response function chi
INPUTHP.description:
Convergence threshold for the response function chi,
which is defined as a trace of the response
occupation matrix.

INPUTHP.name: thresh_init
INPUTHP.label: Threshold for the 1st iteration of the linear system
INPUTHP.description:
Initial threshold for the solution of the linear
system (first iteration). Needed to converge the
bare (non-interacting) response function chi0.
The specified value will be multiplied by the
number of electrons in the system.

INPUTHP.name: ethr_nscf
INPUTHP.label: Threshold for the convergence of eigenvalues in NSCF
INPUTHP.description:
Threshold for the convergence of eigenvalues during
the iterative diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in
the non-self-consistent-field (NSCF) calculation at
k and k+q points. Note, this quantity is NOT extensive.

INPUTHP.name: niter_max
INPUTHP.label: Maximum number of iterations for linear-response calc.
INPUTHP.description:
Maximum number of iterations in the iterative
solution of the linear-response Kohn-Sham equations.

INPUTHP.name: alpha_mix
INPUTHP.label: Mixing parameter (alpha_mix(1))
INPUTHP.description:
Mixing parameter (for the i-th iteration) for updating
the response SCF potential using the modified Broyden
method. See: D.D. Johnson, "PRB 38, 12807 (1988)".

INPUTHP.name: nmix
INPUTHP.label: Number of iterations to use in Broyden mixing

INPUTHP.name: num_neigh
INPUTHP.label: Number of neighbors of every Hubbard atom to consider for V
INPUTHP.description:
Number of nearest neighbors of every Hubbard atom which
will be considered when writting Hubbard V parameters to
the file parameters.out, which can be used in the
subsequent DFT+U+V calculation. This keyword is used only
for DFT+U+V (post-processing stage).

INPUTHP.name: lmin
INPUTHP.label: Minimum orbital quantum number of the Hubbard atoms
INPUTHP.description:
Minimum value of the orbital quantum number of the Hubbard
atoms starting from which (and up to the maximum l in the
system) Hubbard V will be written to the file parameters.out.
"lmin" refers to the orbital quantum number of the atom
corresponding to the first site-index in Hubbard_V(:,:,:).
This keyword is used only for DFT+U+V and only
in the post-processing stage. Example: "lmin"=1 corresponds to
writing to file V between e.g. oxygen (with p states) and its
neighbors, and including V between transition metals (with d
states) and their neighbors. Instead, when "lmin"=2 only the
latter will be written to parameters.out.

INPUTHP.name: rmax
INPUTHP.label: Maximum neighbor distance (in Bohr) between two atoms
INPUTHP.description:
Maximum distance (in Bohr) between two atoms to search
neighbors (used only at the postprocessing step for
DFT+U+V). This keyword is useful when there
are e.g. defects in the system.

INPUTHP.name: dist_thr
INPUTHP.label: Threshold (in Bohr) for comparing inter-atomic distances
INPUTHP.description:
Threshold (in Bohr) for comparing inter-atomic distances
when reconstructing the missing elements of the response
susceptibility in the post-processing step.

PATH.name: string_method
PATH.label: Type of path calculation
PATH.description:
A string describing the task to be performed. Options are:

'neb' :

nudget-elastic-band

'smd' :

string-method-dynamics

PATH.name: restart_mode
PATH.label: Restart mode
PATH.description:
Options are:

'from_scratch' :

from scratch

'restart' :

from previous interrupted run

PATH.name: num_of_images
PATH.label: Number of images used to discretize the path
PATH.description:
Number of points used to discretize the path
(it must be larger than 3).

PATH.name: opt_scheme
PATH.label: Type of optimization scheme
PATH.description:
Specify the type of optimization scheme:

'sd' :

steepest descent

'broyden' :

quasi-Newton Broyden's second method (suggested)

'broyden2' :

another variant of the quasi-Newton Broyden's
second method to be tested and compared with the
previous one.

'quick-min' :

an optimisation algorithm based on the
projected velocity Verlet scheme

'langevin' :

finite temperature langevin dynamics of the
string (smd only). It is used to compute the
average path and the free-energy profile.

PATH.name: CI_scheme
PATH.label: Type of climbing image scheme
PATH.description:
Specify the type of Climbing Image scheme:

'no-CI' :

climbing image is not used

'auto' :

original CI scheme. The image highest in energy
does not feel the effect of springs and is
allowed to climb along the path

'manual' :

images that have to climb are manually selected.
See also "CLIMBING_IMAGES" card

PATH.name: first_last_opt
PATH.label: Optimize also the first and the last configurations
PATH.description:
Also the first and the last configurations are optimized
"on the fly" (these images do not feel the effect of the springs).

PATH.name: minimum_image
PATH.label: Use a minimum image criterion
PATH.description:
Assume a "minimum image criterion" to build the path. If an atom
moves by more than half the length of a crystal axis between one
image and the next in the input (before interpolation),
an appropriate periodic replica of that atom is chosen.
Useful to avoid jumps in the initial reaction path.

PATH.name: temp_req
PATH.label: Temperature used for langevin dynamics of the string
PATH.description: Temperature used for the langevin dynamics of the string.

PATH.name: ds
PATH.label: Optimization step length
PATH.description:
Optimisation step length ( Hartree atomic units ).
If "opt_scheme"=="broyden", ds is used as a guess for the
diagonal part of the Jacobian matrix.

PATH.name: path_thr
PATH.label: Convergence threshold for path optimization
PATH.description:
The simulation stops when the error ( the norm of the force
orthogonal to the path in eV/A ) is less than path_thr.

PATH.name: use_freezing
PATH.label: Only the images with larger errors are optimised
PATH.description:
If. TRUE. the images are optimised according to their error:
only those images with an error larger than half of the largest
are optimised. The other images are kept frozen.

PATH.name: use_masses
PATH.label: The optimisation is done with mass-weighted coordinates
PATH.description:
If. TRUE. the optimisation of the path is performed using
mass-weighted coordinates. Useful together with quick-min
optimization scheme, if some bonds are much stiffer than
others. By assigning a larger (fictitious) mass to atoms
with stiff bonds, one may use a longer time step "ds"

PATH.name: lfcp
PATH.label: Perform a constant bias potential calculation using ESM
PATH.description:
If .TRUE. perform a constant bias potential (constant-mu) calculation with
- ESM method (assume_isolated = 'esm' and esm_bc = 'bc2' or 'bc3' must be
set in SYSTEM namelist) or
- ESM-RISM method (assume_isolated = 'esm' and esm_bc = 'bc1' must be set
set in SYSTEM namelist, and trism = .TRUE. must be set
set in CONTROL namelist).

"fcp_mu" gives the target Fermi energy.
See the header of PW/src/fcp_module.f90 for documentation

PATH.name: fcp_mu
PATH.label: Target Fermi energy in Ry
PATH.description:
If "lfcp" == .TRUE., gives the target Fermi energy [eV].
One can specify the total charge of the system for the first
and last image by giving "TOTAL_CHARGE" cards
so that the Fermi energy of these systems will be the target value,
otherwise "first_last_opt" should be .TRUE.
For the initial charge of intermediate images, the "TOTAL_CHARGE"
is linearly interpolated between the initial and the final ones
unless the "TOTAL_CHARGE" is given in the input file.

PATH.name: fcp_thr
PATH.label: Convergence threshold for FCP force
PATH.description:
The simulation stops when the error ( the maximum of the force
acting on the FCP in V ) is less than fcp_thr.

PATH.name: fcp_scheme
PATH.label: Type of FCP optimization scheme
PATH.description:
Specify the type of optimization scheme for FCP:

'lm' :

Line-Minimization method.

'newton' :

Newton-Raphson method with diagonal hessian matrix.
Also, coupling with DIIS.

'coupled' :

Coupled method with ionic positions.
This is available only if "opt_scheme" == 'broyden',
or 'broyden2'.
